model: Insurer FCFE at cost of equity, BVPS-compounding calibrated (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR (22.4%) and EPS/net-income 3-yr CAGRs (35-39%) are measured off the FY2022 trough (Hurricane Ian, $1.6B AOCI bond mark-down that depressed equity to $8.4B) and include the May-2023 $1.5B equity raise; they are not sustainable rates. Revenue 5-yr CAGR of 12.8% reflects the 2021-2024 hard-market expansion that management is now deliberately reversing (FY2026 revenue shrinking). The per-share book-value CAGR (8.2% over 10 years, 9.6% over 5) is the only series that describes what a shareholder actually compounded, and is the selected rate. 'fcf' CAGRs are computed on GAAP net income (the distributable-earnings proxy for an insurer), not reported OCF.
historical_growth.notes: BVPS approximated as period-end equity / weighted diluted shares for FY2015 (~$173) and FY2020 (~$243), and equity / cover-page shares for FY2025 (~$383). Year-end P/B history (FY2015-FY2025): 1.06, 1.12, 1.09, 1.13, 1.24, 0.97, 1.08, 1.54 (FY2022 AOCI-depressed book), 1.16, 1.12, 0.89; now 0.93x on $399 BVPS at 2026-06-30.

scenario_narratives.base: Everest completes its 2025-26 reset: the AIG retail book runs off, property-cat capacity is cut into 15-20% rate declines, and revenue troughs around $15.7B in FY2027 before growing 2-3% a year. Core Reinsurance Treaty and Global Wholesale & Specialty run a ~90% combined ratio; adding a normal cat load and the Legacy segment's drag gives a group CR of ~94% and, with $2.2-2.5B of net investment income, a 13% pre-tax margin and ~11% ROE from FY2028. FY2026 earns ~$2.0B (H1 actual $1.2B plus a cat- and reserve-review-laden H2), a little below the street's ~$54 EPS. Equity/revenue is held at ~0.95x, so about a quarter of earnings is retained and the rest returned through the $8/share dividend and buybacks. Exit at ~1.1x book, Everest's 10-year median.
scenario_narratives.bull: The $1.2B adverse development cover and the exit from retail casualty genuinely draw a line under US casualty reserves; no further charges emerge and rating outlooks return to stable. Core underwriting stays at a 90% combined ratio, NII keeps compounding as the portfolio reinvests above 4.5%, and from FY2028 capital freed from the retail book is redeployed into specialty and casualty reinsurance at 4-5% growth. Margins of 15% deliver 13-14% ROE, three points above the cost of equity, and the market re-rates the stock to ~1.35x book as it did in 2019 and 2023.
scenario_narratives.bear: Social inflation keeps running ahead of Everest's picks and a third consecutive Q4 reserve charge (~$400-500M) lands in FY2026; AM Best or S&P downgrade to A, and cedents trim Everest's share on large treaties. Property-cat pricing stays soft through 2028 while alternative capital keeps flooding in, so revenue shrinks to ~$15B and stays there. A 10% pre-tax margin is an ~8% ROE, below the 10% cost of equity, and the stock stays priced as a value-destroying compounder at ~0.8x book -- roughly where it closed FY2025.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Everest is a compounder of book value, so it is valued as one: the distributable-earnings stream (pre-tax income after interest, less tax and less the capital retained to support premium volume) is discounted at a 10% cost of equity with net debt held at zero, and the terminal value is capped so each scenario exits at a price-to-book consistent with Everest's own history (0.8x / 1.1x / 1.35x). The question the model answers is whether a reinsurer earning ~11% on equity through the cycle, returning ~9% of its market cap a year, deserves to trade at 0.93x book. Reported OCF, EBITDA and P/E are not used: for a reinsurer OCF is float movement, EBITDA is undefined, and a trailing P/E of ~8x on a year with $1.7B of reserve charges says little.
key_risks_to_valuation: Reserve adequacy: every $500M of further US casualty adverse development is ~$11/share of book and, more importantly, evidence that the 13% normalised margin is too high -- the bear path, not a one-off.
Exit multiple: roughly half of base-case value is the year-10 exit at 1.09x book; at the FY2025 low of 0.89x the base IV falls by ~$35/share.
Catastrophe and geopolitical losses: a 1-in-100 cat year has historically taken Everest's ROE to ~1-5% (2017, 2018, 2020) and would remove a year of the compounding the model assumes.
Pricing cycle: property-cat rates down 15-20% at 2026 renewals; if casualty and specialty follow, the 13% margin is unattainable and the model converges on the bear case.
Rate sensitivity: ~$2.3B of net investment income on a $40B+ fixed-income book; a 100bp fall in reinvestment yields is ~$300-400M of pre-tax income over time (~2pp of margin).

Share count: the model holds 38.5M shares flat and treats buybacks as the distribution of the FCFE it values; it does not add value for buying back stock below book, which is a modest source of conservatism at 0.93x.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 302.44-401.07.
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 1095073) via scripts/build_facts_xbrl.py into core_metrics/EG_Metrics.csv (FY2008-Q2 2026); Q2-2026 10-Q (filed 2026-08-03) for equity $15,430M, senior notes $2,352M, cover-page shares 38,342,734 (2026-07-27), diluted weighted 38.8M, H1-2026 pre-tax income $1,420M and tax $207M; FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-26) for revenue $17,496M, pre-tax $1,887M, tax $296M, SBC $61M, buybacks $797M, dividends $335M.
data_sources.qualitative: EG_Analysis.json (2026-09-28): 2025 segment recast, AIG renewal-rights sale, $1.2B ADC, FY2024/FY2025 adverse development, Oct-2025 negative outlooks, Q2-2026 results and management commentary on pricing discipline.

inputs.share_count_basis: 38.34M common shares on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover (2026-07-27) plus ~0.15M dilutive equity awards (Q2-2026 diluted weighted average 38.8M vs basic ~38.65M). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed inside the pre-tax margin and buybacks are the use of the FCFE being valued, so shrinking the count as well would double-count the capital return.
inputs.debt_note: Everest carries $2,352M of senior notes (10-Q 2026-06-30, us-gaap:SeniorNotes) plus ~$218M of long-term subordinated notes due 2067. They are operating capital for a reinsurer and their interest is already deducted inside pre-tax income (the flow this model capitalises at the cost of equity), so net debt is held at ZERO in the bridge -- subtracting it again would deduct the debt twice. Recorded here for the reader; not an input to value.
inputs.fcf_basis_note: This is not a cash-flow-statement FCF. reported_fcf = FY2025 GAAP net income $1,591M + $61M SBC add-back (earnings before SBC); last_fcf = FY2025 net income $1,591M, the distributable-earnings (FCFE) base the model projects. Reported OCF ($3,068M FY2025) is float and reserve movement, not owner cash, and is deliberately not used.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement share-based compensation add-back ($61M, core_metrics stock_based_comp). Equity-award withholding taxes ($22M FY2025, kpis equity_award_taxes) are NOT added: for an insurer they are economically part of the buyback programme, not an unexpensed cost. Net investment income is the operating engine of a reinsurer, not surplus-cash interest, so interest_income is 0.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:02Z regular close (latest close; fetched pre-market 2026-09-28, not an after-hours print)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY, not WACC: the flows are post-interest FCFE. USD build: 10-yr UST ~4.2% + reinsurer equity beta ~1.1 x ERP ~5.3% = ~10.0%. The 1.1 beta (vs a ~0.7 trailing market beta) reflects fundamental earnings volatility -- Everest's ROE has ranged 1% to 19% across the last decade on cat years and reserve charges -- and matches the ~10% cost of equity reinsurers and their rating agencies conventionally use. No further scenario or ratings-outlook premium is stacked on top; the reserve and pricing risks are carried in the bear scenario's margin path and its 25% weight, so risk is charged once. The SAME 10% applies to all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: operating leases are immaterial for a reinsurer (office space only) and are already expensed inside pre-tax income.
inputs.nci_treatment: Not applicable: no material non-controlling interests; Mt. Logan Re third-party capital is accounted for as reinsurance ceded / funds held, not NCI.
inputs.notes: MODEL: routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Insurer, holdco, compounder-of-book -> BVPS compounding x exit P/B'. Everest genuinely compounds book (equity $7.6B FY2015 -> $15.4B Jun-2026 while paying $1.92->$8.00 DPS and retiring ~13% of shares; BVPS ~$173 -> ~$399, 8.2% 10-yr CAGR), so that row applies rather than the IAG.AX override. To get validated dashboard sliders and the generated workbook the book-compounding logic is expressed on the FCFE-at-cost-of-equity engine route (same family as NAB.AX/IAG.AX): 'revenue' = total revenues (premiums earned + net investment income + realised gains); 'EBITDA margin' = pre-tax income before SBC as % of revenue (so pre-tax income is post-interest and post-cats); D&A = 0; cash tax = 15% (Bermuda CIT 15% effective 2025; FY2025 GAAP rate 15.7%, H1-2026 14.6%); 'capex' = RETAINED CAPITAL needed to hold equity/revenue at ~0.95x while premiums grow (retention = 0.95 x revenue growth; 1.5% of revenue in the shrinking FY26-27 years because management is still retaining ~25% of earnings to placate three negative rating-agency outlooks rather than releasing capital); working capital = 0; net debt = 0. The terminal_cap_multiple is set per scenario so the implied exit value lands on an exit P/B consistent with Everest's own 10-yr year-end P/B history (0.89-1.24x ex the FY2022 AOCI outlier, median ~1.10x): bear ~0.8x, base ~1.1x, bull ~1.35x book at year 10. The engine's owner-FCF identity still holds (last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income) but the quantities are earnings-based, see fcf_basis_note. Reinsurer-specific: FY0 = FY2025; FY2026 revenue falls ~7.5% as the AIG retail renewal-rights sale (~$2B GWP) runs off and management shrinks property-cat lines into 15-20% rate declines (H1-2026 revenue -8.3% YoY); H1-2026 pre-tax margin of 17.7% is a clean half and is NOT carried forward -- H2 carries a normal Q3 cat load and a Q4 reserve review (Q3-2025 $361M and Q4-2025 further US casualty strengthening), so FY2026 base pre-tax+SBC margin is 14.8% (~$2.0B net income, ~13% ROE, a little below the ~$54 street EPS implied by the 6.8x forward P/E). Normalised margin 13% from FY2028 = ~11% ROE, close to the 10-yr average ROE of ~10% lifted by the exit from retail casualty and structurally higher NII; that sits 1pp above the 10% cost of equity, which is why fair P/B is a little above 1.0x. House and street bases differ only by the tiny 0.35%-of-revenue SBC charge; the band is narrow, not collapsed.

bear.rationale: A third year of US casualty adverse development (~$400-500M in Q4-2026, taking FY2026 margin to 12%), a rating downgrade to A that costs cedent share, and a soft property-cat market lasting through 2028. 10% normalised margin = ~8% ROE, below the cost of equity, so the 10x cap pins the exit at ~0.8x book, near the FY2025 low. Capex 1.0% in FY2028-29 recognises a downgraded, shrinking reinsurer retains less.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 -7.5%: H1-2026 revenue -8.3% YoY as the AIG retail renewal-rights book runs off and property-cat is shrunk into softer pricing; FY2027 -3% as the run-off completes and property rates fall a further 10-15%; then 2-3% nominal growth (exposure growth + NII on a growing portfolio) fading to 2.5%.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax income + SBC as % of revenue. H1-2026 actual 17.7% (clean half, core CR 90%); FY2025 11.2% (with $1.7B adverse development); FY2024 9.0% (with $1.3B). FY2026 14.8% = H1 actual + an H2 with a normal cat load and a modest Q4 reserve top-up. FY2027 12.5% for a soft property market. 13.0% normalised = group CR ~94% incl. cats and Legacy drag plus ~$2.2-2.5B NII less ~$150M interest; equals ~11% ROE.
base.capex_rationale: Retained capital: equity/revenue held at ~0.95x, so retention = 0.95 x growth (1.9% at 2% growth, 2.85% at 3%, 2.4% at 2.5%). 1.5% in FY2026-27 despite shrinking revenue because management is still retaining ~25% of earnings while three rating agencies hold negative outlooks.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 10%/2.5% = 13.7x FCFE would imply ~1.19x book at year 10; the 12.5x cap binds and pins the exit at ~1.09x book, the 10-yr median year-end P/B. Steady-state (ROE-g)/(CoE-g) = (11-2.5)/(10-2.5) = 1.13x corroborates.

bull.rationale: Reserve line holds (the $1.2B ADC and re-underwriting end US casualty charges), core CR stays ~90%, NII compounds on a $40B+ portfolio, and capital freed from retail insurance is redeployed into specialty/casualty reinsurance at hard-ish rates from FY2028. 15% margin = ~13-14% ROE; 13.5x cap pins exit at ~1.35x book, near the FY2019/FY2023 peaks.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12.5x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25%: two consecutive years of nine-figure-plus US casualty adverse development ($1.3B FY2024, $1.7B FY2025), negative outlooks from all three rating agencies since Oct-2025, and a property-cat market that management itself says stays soft into 2027 -- reserve risk is a thesis-level uncertainty, not a tail. Bull cut to 25%: it needs three independent things to go right at once (no further reserve charges, pricing holding in casualty/specialty, and a P/B re-rating that the market has denied the stock for eighteen months). Base 50% because the FY2026 numbers already in hand (H1 $1.2B net income, $725M buybacks) are tracking the base path.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
